page: Amazon Web Services i8ge.metal-48xl is a bare-metal, storage-optimized server powered by AWS Graviton processors. It features 192 dedicated physical cores built on the ARMv9 Neoverse-V2 architecture, operating at a clock speed of 2.7 GHz. The system is configured with 1536.0 GB of high-speed DDR5 memory, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per core, and is backed by a baseline network bandwidth of 300 Gbps. It includes a massive local storage capacity of 120,000 GB of NVMe SSDs, with no integrated GPUs.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates top-tier multi-core and memory performance. It ranks in the top 10% for multi-core stress-ng CPU tests, multi-threaded bzip3 decompression, and software compilation with Clang. Memory bandwidth is exceptionally strong, with cached read-only bandwidth reaching 13,947.51 GB/sec and uncached write bandwidth at 258.51 GB/sec. Database operations and Redis SET operations also perform in the top tier, with Redis handling 378.59 million operations per second. However, single-core performance and text generation for large language models are relatively average or poor.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the i8ge.metal-48xl offers high resource density by combining massive local NVMe storage with a high-core-count ARM architecture. This configuration reduces the necessity for external block storage attachments, optimizing costs for data-intensive deployments. The primary tradeoff lies in its single-threaded performance and the lack of hardware acceleration for GPU-dependent workloads, making it less suitable for deep learning training or heavy single-core computations.

This server is highly suited for large-scale database deployments, high-throughput Redis caching layers, distributed storage systems, and intensive data processing pipelines. It is also well-suited for multi-threaded software compilation and high-volume static web serving.
